name: Krio
notes: Krio, English-lexifier creole of Sierra Leone (5-10% native speakers, lingua franca for the whole country). Orthography adds the African-reference-alphabet letters ⟨ɛ⟩, ⟨ɔ⟩, ⟨ŋ⟩ to the Latin alphabet minus ⟨q x⟩; a standardised orthography exists but is not universally followed, and phonetic/phonemic transcription remains common (Finney, APiCS ch. 15). ⟨kp⟩ /k͡p/ and ⟨gb⟩ /ɡ͡b/ are labial-velar co-articulated stops from West African substrate languages, one segment each, not clusters. ⟨r⟩ is the uvular fricative /ʁ/, not an alveolar. ⟨ny⟩ = /ɲ/. The three diphthongs /ai au ɔi/ are written ⟨ay aw ɔy⟩. All seven vowels can be nasalised; nasalisation is largely predictable (an oral vowel before a nasal consonant that then deletes, chiefly in English-derived words) so it is recorded as an allophone rather than a written contrast, since Krio's practical orthography does not mark it. Krio is also a tone language (contrastive LL/LH/HL/HH on both African- and English-derived words), but tone marks are not used in normal orthography and are omitted here, matching the citing source.

Declared with no phonemes because id-keyed overlay replaces a parent rule but cannot delete it.

location.notes: Freetown, Sierra Leone — Glottolog's representative point for Krio.

ancestors.notes: English lexifier, chiefly via the language of Black settlers/Nova Scotian and Maroon returnees who founded Freetown (1787-1800). Finney, APiCS ch. 15.
Yoruba substrate/adstrate via the large recaptive (liberated-African) population resettled in Freetown after 1808.
Mande-area substrate influence (e.g. labial-velar stops kp/gb) shared with other West-African-coast English creoles.
